title: Formats other tools depend on, and text the licence forbids rewriting

census.why: There is no CSV extractor, so the sweep reads the file and forces its header row into the inventory as `unclassified`. That is the design working: the bytes are LISTED, and G2 refuses to pass until somebody decides. A tool that silently skipped `.csv` would report this repository clean.
Same mechanism on a different unsupported extension, and a reminder that `.example` files are committed precisely so a human reads them.
Extensionless. It has to be READ in order to be protected — a rule saying 'never translate this file' cannot fire on a file no extractor ever opened.
Vendored, and matched by path rather than by name.
The code that names the same columns the CSV does.

expectations.why: The correct answer is `surfaced`, NOT `do-not-translate`, and writing that down is the whole point of the case. The engine has no CSV reader, so it cannot know these are column names another tool consumes — it can only refuse to pretend. Translating this header breaks every import that has ever consumed the export.
Data, not copy. `actif` is a stored value that looks exactly like a French adjective, because it is one.
A connection string surfaced by the sweep. Human-looking enough to be found, and not a sentence.

expectations.find: Copiez ce fichier en .env avant de démarrer le serveur.
expectations.why: Genuinely a French sentence a reader sees, and still `unclassified`, because no extractor claimed the file. The honest report is 'found, not understood' rather than a verdict the engine has no grounds for.

expectations.find: Permission is hereby granted, free of charge
expectations.why: `hard` is the load-bearing field: no agent verdict may override it. Altering LICENSE breaks GitHub's licence detection and the repository starts displaying 'Other'.

expectations.find: Redistribution and use in source and binary forms
expectations.why: Matched by its path rather than its name. Somebody else's licence, and not ours to restate.
Negotiated with a server. The header NAME beside it is equally untouchable, and equally English-looking.
The same French words as the CSV header, here as an array of column names. `nom` and `statut` are ordinary French nouns AND an interop contract; only their use decides, and it is in another file.
A button label sitting one line below the column names it exports. Same file, same language, opposite treatment.

knownGaps: `'Content-Type'`, `'Accept-Language'` and `'XMLHttpRequest'` come back needs-judgment/ambiguous-role rather than as the API contract they are. Refused, so nothing breaks — but by a generic hesitation rather than by recognising an HTTP header, so a longer header name in the same object would read as copy.
`'fr-FR'` lands on needs-judgment/ambiguous-role. It is a locale marker in a header map, which is the one thing in this file that SHOULD be retargeted rather than left alone; the engine sees neither.
